clue.text: Isn't it safe to go round it?

definitions.text: Isn't it safe to go round it?

parts.words: Isn't it safe to go round it?
parts.note: a bend in the road where driving round is hazardous; the question form teases that it is not safe to negotiate

explanation.walkthrough: The question looks like a puzzle about safety in general; it describes a hazardous bend on a road. It is also the title of a J. B. Priestley play.
explanation.definitionFit: A bend that is perilous to drive round is by its nature not safe to take.

clue.text: Draws vassal and vessel using skill on board

parts.note: draughts are drawings or sketches, things drawn
a vassal is a feudal man, a liegeman
a vessel is a ship

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a serf and a boat while playing a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' points to the game of draughts (checkers), played on a board, while the answer's main sense is skill at drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Proficiency in technical drawing, punningly also expertise at the board game draughts.

clue.text: Either way it's off

indicators.note: read forwards or backwards the letters of the answer are the same, so it works in both directions

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever direction you look at it, the plan is cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unacceptable or cancelled is said to be off, in colloquial use.

clue.text: Loosely fondles or embraces

indicators.note: done loosely, the letters of fondles are arranged in a free new order

explanation.surface: Someone casually caresses or hugs a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap up or hold within one's arms is to hug or clasp.

clue.text: Alternative place in Somerset where trees are grown

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
Chard is a town in Somerset, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Another spot in the West Country where trees are cultivated.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARD is a small market town in Somerset; Somerset is famous for apple growing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plot planted with fruit-bearing trees such as apples.

clue.text: Opens out assorted drapes on Sunday

indicators.note: assorted means mixed up, so the letters of drapes are jumbled

explanation.surface: On a Sunday someone unfolds various curtains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assorted' rearranges DRAPES to SPREAD, then S for Sunday follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfold or extend something across a surface.

clue.text: Lake province

explanation.surface: A lake that is also a province.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America shares its name with a Canadian province.

clue.text: Again a cur is removed from the country

indicators.note: removed here means moved again, so the letters of again a cur are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A stray dog is once more taken out of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' is read as re-moved, signalling an anagram of AGAIN A CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic in Central America is a country.

clue.text: Old king at St Andrews?

parts.note: old suggests ancient and king suggests royal, and the governing golf club based at St Andrews in Scotland bears both words

explanation.walkthrough: The Royal and Ancient Golf Club at St Andrews in Scotland has long governed the rules of golf; the clue reads like a monarch visiting the town.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous golf club in the Scottish town combines words meaning regal and very old.

clue.text: One contriving to be a craftsman

explanation.surface: A schemer turns out to be a skilled worker.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventor or deviser, and also a skilled mechanic or maker.

clue.text: Gaudy tintack you held

indicators.note: held means the letters are contained within the phrase tintack you

explanation.surface: A showy drawing pin that you are holding.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and cheap-looking, in poor taste.

clue.text: Group with back trouble at nerve-centres

parts.note: a gang is a group of people

indicators.note: back here signals that the word for trouble runs backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A team suffering from back problems at the nerve centres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the body part, but it reverses AIL to LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Clusters of nerve cells acting as relay points in the nervous system.

clue.text: Of Dawn or Laura in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance changed, so the letters of or Laura are rearranged

explanation.surface: Either a girl named Dawn or one called Laura wearing a disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn' looks like a woman's name beside Laura but is the definition: the Latin goddess Aurora is the dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to daybreak, from Aurora the Roman goddess of morning.

clue.text: Shade left of centre

explanation.surface: A political colour on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour or hue, and politically socialist or left-leaning.

clue.text: Braided sweet was sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the word for sweet is turned round

parts.note: a sweet is a pudding or dessert

explanation.surface: A plaited pudding was returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' reverses DESSERT, the course called sweet in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the hair arranged in plaits or long locks.

clue.text: Give information going round in the glen

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters of in the glen circulate into a new order

explanation.surface: A guide passes on facts while walking around the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct or inform someone, making them understand.

clue.text: And the rest is a bit sketchy

indicators.note: a bit of a word means a short run of its letters

explanation.surface: The remainder is somewhat vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for et cetera, Latin for and so on.

clue.text: Unusually noughts might be coming from this instead of blanks?

definitions.text: might be coming from this instead of blanks?

indicators.note: unusually means not in the normal way, so the letters of noughts are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, zeros rather than blank cartridges might emerge from a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NOUGHTS gives the weapon, which normally fires shot rather than blanks; noughts suggests the scattering of pellets.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-bore gun fires pellets of shot rather than harmless blank cartridges.

clue.text: Ben takes nothing less than 60 minutes

indicators.note: less means the zero letter is taken away from the word for sixty minutes

parts.note: sixty minutes make an hour
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Ben needs well under an hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ben' is the definition through the film and novel Ben-Hur, whose second word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben-Hur is the hero of Lew Wallace's novel, so the name follows Ben.

clue.text: Mother left bill with accountant for cane

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
AC is short for account, a bill
CA stands for chartered accountant

explanation.surface: Mum set off for the bank leaving an invoice for her accountant about a walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: AC (account) is the bill; CA (chartered accountant) the accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking stick made from the stem of a rattan palm, named after the Malaysian port.

clue.text: Rush during short visit about a set of principles

indicators.note: during places the word for rush inside the shortened visit
short means the word for visit loses its last letter

parts.note: a call is a short visit
a rush is a reed-like marsh plant

explanation.surface: Hurrying through a brief stop concerning someone's beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts CALL to CAL; 'during' puts REED inside. 'Rush' looks like haste but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a creed, a formal statement of religious belief.

clue.text: The definite item

explanation.surface: A specific object.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'the' is the definite article in grammar; an article is also an object or thing.

clue.text: A garden had been cultivated on the island

indicators.note: cultivated soil is turned over, so the letters of a garden are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone tended a plot on a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Caribbean island nation in the Windward Islands.

clue.text: Little room with Stan jumping — he's athletic

parts.note: gym is the shortened form of gymnasium, a room for exercise

indicators.note: jumping suggests the letters of Stan leap about into another order

explanation.surface: Stan leaps around a small room, showing he is sporty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the short form GYM of gymnasium, a room; 'jumping' turns STAN into NAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trained in physical exercises such as vaulting and tumbling.

clue.text: Outshine despite the loss of light

explanation.surface: Something surpasses others although darkness falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass or overshadow, and the blocking of the sun or moon's light by another body.

clue.text: Little hope of some sunshine

explanation.surface: A small chance of a bit of sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A glimmer, as in a slight chance of success, and a single beam of light.

clue.text: Do not notice the uncared-for state

explanation.surface: Ignoring the poor condition of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: To fail to attend to something, and the condition of being left untended.

clue.text: Man provided backing with large number doing mischief

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: backing means the word for provided is reversed

parts.note: if means provided that
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a large number

explanation.surface: A man offering support with a big crowd causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but reverses IF to FI; C, the Roman hundred, is the large number.
explanation.definitionFit: Causing harm or evil; maleficent.

clue.text: Composition played loudly before mid-January with half the guests

parts.note: F stands for forte, loudly in music

indicators.note: mid takes the central letter of January
half the word guests means its first three letters

explanation.surface: A piece played forte at a party in January with half the guests present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-January' gives U, the middle letter of JANUARY; 'half the guests' gives GUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrapuntal musical piece in which a theme is taken up by successive voices.

clue.text: Had not liked what Edward had included

indicators.note: included means the letters sit inside the words what Edward

explanation.surface: Someone disliked what Edward had put in.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested or loathed, past tense to match had not liked.

clue.text: Bubbly enjoyed by a hypochondriac, it's said

indicators.note: it's said means the words are heard spoken, giving a word with a similar sound

parts.note: a hypochondriac relishes sham pain, an imagined ailment

explanation.surface: Fizzy wine relished by someone who imagines illness.
explanation.walkthrough: A hypochondriac enjoys sham (fake) pain; said aloud that sounds like the sparkling wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly is informal for sparkling wine from France.

clue.text: Paying one's fine in convicts' home?

explanation.surface: Settling a court fine at a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically, paying a court penalty is a penal settlement; really it is a colony where convicts were sent, such as early Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying a legal penalty settles it, and a colony for transported prisoners was such a settlement.
